Subject: Onsite deployment addendum — initial scope/questions

Hi Monica / Dev,

Thanks for the demo last week — MedTech is excited about moving forward with a private, onsite deployment for our inference workloads. Before we proceed to procurement, our legal and security teams have a couple of specific asks so our GC can approve the MSA + Order Form:

1) License scope: we need explicit language that Redwood's license to run the model in-customer-premises excludes any claim over customer-owned models or derivatives produced from customer data.
2) Audit & evidence: we require an audit clause that allows one SOC-like evidence package annually and ad-hoc compliance checks with 30 days notice. We may ask for more granular logs (audit log samples, KV cache handling) to satisfy our auditors.
3) Escrow/exit: our procurement team asked whether Redwood offers an escrow or code deposit for the runtime in case of termination — or at least a signed attestation regarding continuations and customer data custody.
4) Subprocessors & location: list of third-party subprocessors and confirmation that processing will remain in our US region.

Can you share a draft addendum and a proposed audit schedule? Aaron from procurement is on copy and will coordinate timelines.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — our board is targeting a March procurement approval window.

Best,
Sarah Chen
Head of Cloud Ops
MedTech Systems

Sarah / Aaron —

Thanks for the clear list. I attached a draft Onsite Addendum (Word) and a redlined MSA (PDF) that attempt to address each of the items below. High-level notes:

- License carve-out: proposed language adds a Customer Model carve-out and clarifies that outputs derived solely from customer data remain the customer's IP. See Section 2.1.b in the attached redline.
- Audit scope: we can commit to an annual evidence package plus up to two ad-hoc checks with 30 days' notice; for any ad-hoc deep-dive we ask for a narrow scope and an approved NDA for auditors. We proposed a sample logs package instead of full production logs to limit exposure.
- Escrow: Redwood does not currently offer source-code escrow for the runtime binary; we provided an attestation template and a runbook extract that can be stored with your legal team. If escrow is a hard requirement, we can engage our legal/ops and present a statement of work for a one-time escrow arrangement.
- Subprocessors & region: attached spreadsheet lists our infra partners; for this engagement we propose US-only regions.

Next steps: can we lock a 60-minute call Wednesday 03/03 with your GC and security lead to walk through the redlines? If that works I’ll schedule and include our Legal (Karthik) + Ops (Dev).

I’ve also uploaded the redlines to the linked Drive folder for comment: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Qz-Onsite-Addendum

Thanks,

Internal — quick tech/legal points to consider before the call with MedTech:

1) License scope tweak (2.1.b): add explicit \"Customer Models\" definition: models trained exclusively on Customer Data or models uploaded by Customer. Avoids ambiguity around derivatives produced by the runtime.
2) Audit evidence: recommend offering a fixed \"evidence bundle\" (hashes of binaries, config snapshot, sample audit logs redacted for PII) plus a signed runbook extract. For ad-hoc audits, require on-site or read-only access via jumpbox under Redwood supervision — and a maximum of two ad-hoc inspections/year.
3) Custody & keys: if MedTech insists on cryptographic custody, propose a bring-your-own-KMS (BYOK) option with a shared-responsibility attestation in the addendum. Otherwise, we allow standard Redwood-managed keys with documented rotation and export restrictions.
4) Escrow alternative: propose a notarized attestation + limited source deposit with an escrow vendor as a paid add-on.

I suggest standing language ready to reduce back-and-forth during the call. I put suggested markup in the attached redline (already in the Drive).

— Dev
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
